api/Invex.Tools.ArtifactClean.Commands.h.summary: Class Commands Namespace Invex.Tools.ArtifactClean Assembly Invex.Tools.ArtifactClean.dll The artclean command set registered with ConsoleAppFramework, which cleans a .NET workspace by running dotnet clean, deleting every bin and obj directory, and optionally running dotnet restore. public sealed class Commands Inheritance object Commands Methods Clean(string?, bool, bool) Runs 'dotnet clean', then recursively deletes 'bin' and 'obj' directories from the specified path, then optionally restores the project. [PublicAPI] [SuppressMessage("Performance", "CA1822:Mark members as static", Justification = "Required by ConsoleAppFramework")] public int Clean(string? path = null, bool noRestore = false, bool verbose = false) Parameters path string -p, The root path to start cleaning from. [Default: Current directory] noRestore bool -n, If true, skips any restore operations. [Default: false] verbose bool -v, If true, outputs detailed information about the cleaning process. [Default: false] Returns int 0 on success; 1 if the path is invalid, 'dotnet clean' or 'dotnet restore' fails, or a 'bin' / 'obj' directory could not be deleted.

The only public type, Commands, is the command plumbing behind artclean and may change without notice. To use the tools, see the Introduction and the ArtifactClean command reference.

docs/artifactclean.html.title: ArtifactClean | Invex .NET Tools
docs/artifactclean.html.summary: ArtifactClean This is the reference for the artclean command. artclean runs dotnet clean, recursively removes bin and obj directories from a .NET workspace, and runs dotnet restore afterward by default. It skips symbolic links, junctions, and other reparse points while traversing. Use this page to look up options, behavior and exit codes. Installation dotnet tool install --global Invex.Tools.ArtifactClean Update an existing installation: dotnet tool update --global Invex.Tools.ArtifactClean ArtifactClean requires .NET 10 and the dotnet command on PATH. Published packages include Native AOT assets for Windows, Linux, and macOS on x64 and ARM64. The workspaces it cleans can target any .NET version. Usage Run from the root of the workspace to clean: artclean Provide a root path to clean a different directory: artclean --path "path/to/workspace" Options Option Description -p, --path <directory> Root directory to clean. Defaults to the current directory. -n, --no-restore Do not run dotnet restore after cleaning. -v, --verbose Show each deleted directory and detailed dotnet output. Skip the restore step, or show each deleted directory and the output of the dotnet commands: artclean --no-restore artclean --verbose The complete command syntax is: artclean [options] -p, --path <directory> Root directory to clean (default: current directory) -n, --no-restore Do not run dotnet restore after cleaning -v, --verbose Show detailed cleanup and dotnet command output Behavioral notes Order. dotnet clean runs first, then the bin / obj deletion, then dotnet restore (unless --no-restore). Both dotnet commands run with the selected directory as their working directory. Matching. Directory names are compared to bin and obj case-insensitively. A matched directory is deleted with all of its contents and is not searched further. Traversal. Symbolic links, junctions and other reparse points are skipped. Directories that cannot be read are skipped silently, or with a message when --verbose is set. Failures. A directory that cannot be deleted is always reported on standard error. Without --verbose, the output of dotnet clean and dotnet restore is hidden, but a failing command is reported with its exit code. Exit codes The tool exits with code 0 on success and 1 when the path does not exist, dotnet clean or dotnet restore fails, or a bin or obj directory cannot be deleted. A failed dotnet clean does not stop the cleanup; the remaining steps still run and the tool reports the failure through its exit code. Warning ArtifactClean permanently deletes all bin and obj directories below the selected path. It skips symbolic links and junctions while traversing the directory tree. See also Getting Started Introduction

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | Invex .NET Tools
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started This guide installs ArtifactClean and runs a first cleanup. It takes a couple of minutes and needs only the .NET SDK. Prerequisites The .NET 10 SDK (dotnet tool install, dotnet clean and dotnet restore are SDK commands) The dotnet command on PATH (ArtifactClean calls dotnet clean and dotnet restore) The workspaces you clean can target any .NET version. Install dotnet tool install --global Invex.Tools.ArtifactClean Check that the command is available: artclean --help To pick up a newer version later, run dotnet tool update --global Invex.Tools.ArtifactClean. Run your first cleanup Warning ArtifactClean permanently deletes every bin and obj directory below the selected path. Run it from, or point it at, the root of the workspace you mean to clean. Change to the root of a .NET workspace (the folder with your .sln, .slnx or project files) and run: artclean The tool prints one line per step: 'dotnet clean' completed successfully. Deleted 12 'bin' / 'obj' directories. 'dotnet restore' completed successfully. To clean another directory without changing to it, pass --path: artclean --path "path/to/workspace" Next steps ArtifactClean: every option, the exact behavior and the exit codes Introduction: when the tool is the right choice and when it is not

docs/introduction.html.title: Introduction | Invex .NET Tools
docs/introduction.html.summary: Introduction Invex .NET Tools is a home for small, single-purpose command-line tools that the Invex team uses while developing .NET code. Each tool is published as its own .NET global tool package. Today the repository ships one tool, ArtifactClean (artclean). What it is Tool Command Package Purpose ArtifactClean artclean Invex.Tools.ArtifactClean Reset a .NET workspace: dotnet clean, delete bin / obj, dotnet restore. When to use ArtifactClean Builds behave strangely after switching branches, SDKs or target frameworks, and dotnet clean alone does not help because stale files sit in obj (for example project.assets.json or generated sources). You want to free disk space taken by build output across many projects under one folder. You want a repeatable "clean slate" step in a local script, with an exit code that says whether it worked. When not to use it To clean a single project in place. dotnet clean (or deleting that one bin / obj folder) is enough. When bin or obj holds something you need. The tool deletes every directory with those names, case-insensitively, below the root, including ones that are not build output. On a directory you did not mean to select. There is no confirmation prompt and deletion is permanent; prefer --path with an explicit workspace root in scripts. Key concepts at a glance Concept Meaning Root path The directory passed with --path, or the current directory. All three steps run against it. Artifact directory Any directory named bin or obj (any casing) below the root. It is deleted with all of its contents. Reparse point A symbolic link, junction or similar. The tool never follows one, so it cannot escape the root or loop. Exit code 0 when every step succeeded, 1 otherwise. Design principles Do one job well. Each tool covers one routine task with as few options as possible. Keep going, then report. A failing step does not abort the rest; the failure shows up in the output and the exit code. Stay inside the root. Links and junctions are skipped so a cleanup never reaches outside the selected tree. Quiet by default. Normal runs print a short summary; detail is opt-in with --verbose. Start fast. Packages include Native AOT builds so a short-lived command does not pay JIT start-up cost. See also Getting Started ArtifactClean
